title: Q3 Inference Runway & Model Health Playbook — Hosted API Roadmap
creator: Priya Patel
description: Quarterly playbook to align product, engineering, and model teams on the Q3 hosted API runway: onboarding approved model variants, defining health signals and gating criteria, scheduling deprecations, and sequencing rollouts to balance latency/cost SLAs. This ticket is the single source of truth for the operational plan that converts roadmap OKRs into tranche-level deliverables and release checks. Emphasis on measurable health indicators (P95 latency, token-cost per request, hallucination/regression flags) and concrete rollback criteria for canary rollouts.
deliverables: Runway plan document with tranche dates and capacity budget by model family
Model health signal catalogue and automated checks for promotion
Deprecation calendar for legacy quantized variants with customer notice templates
Rollout playbook (canary percentages, monitoring hooks, automatic fallback)
Console dashboard widgets for model-level cost/latency/quality and alert thresholds
Hand-off checklist for Support and Success teams with troubleshooting steps
milestones: 2026-04-01: Finalize model candidate list and gating thresholds
2026-04-15: Engineering scope for telemetry and rollout infra confirmed
2026-05-05: First canary tranche (5%) for new curation of text-generation models
2026-05-20: Health signal baseline window complete and alerts configured
2026-06-10: Second tranche (25%) and deprecation announcement published
2026-06-30: Full rollout or rollback decision for remaining traffic; close runway
acceptance_criteria: All model candidates have passing gating checks against synthetic evals and latency budgets
Telemetry for P50/P95/P99 latency, token costs, and quality regressions is visible in Console
Canary rollback succeeds automatically when any critical threshold is breached
Customer-facing deprecation notices are published 30 days before any breaking removal
Runway capacity plan has signed capacity commitments from infra and Dedicated teams
risks: Unexpected latency regressions on long-context workloads leading to SLA breaches
Model quality regressions not caught by existing eval prompts (blind spots)
Insufficient Dedicated capacity for peak burst traffic causing failed rollouts
Customer pushback on deprecation timing for widely used model variants
Telemetry gaps across regions (APAC) could hide region-specific failures
decisions: Promote only quantized variants with end-to-end perf/quality parity within 5% of baseline
Use 3-stage rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on three signal types (latency, cost spike, quality regression)
Require synthetic eval pass plus stochastic sampling QA before any hosted model promotion
Coordinate deprecations with Managed/Dedicated customers via targeted outreach and grace periods
open_questions: What is the minimum size of the synthetic eval corpus to surface hallucination regressions reliably?
Can Dedicated pools provide burst capacity guarantees for tranche dates or do we need alternate routing?
Is there appetite to offer a 'compatibility tier' for customers to opt into older quantized variants for 60 days post-deprecation?
Do we need legal review for customer-facing deprecation language in regulated industries?
